scope: Independent truth and reasoning only; no edits or whole-book acceptance
fresh_context: No target author decision ledger, defense, handoff or prior verdict was read. The review began from the neutral task and actual source text. Earlier authored Chapters 5/6 were not used as authority for these judgments.

initial_and_scope_checks.assessment: Chapter 3 adds a local information measure, a diffusion constraint and a readout cost to the preceding projection model. Chapter 4 needs this only after its separate recording/calibration evidence has established what movement can reveal. Keeping theory before the application gives meaning to the later integrator calculation. An experiment-first order is plausible but would require moving the projection and diffusion prerequisites into the application. No chapter swap is warranted by the connected text.

The baseline is undergraduate calculus, probability and linear algebra. Earlier proposed foundations teaches spikes/rates, conditional Poisson noise, covariance, CV, a continuous attractor and Brownian displacement. Proposed Chapter 2 teaches tangent/left projection, 2D=sum(v_i^2 r_i), u=tau r-prime, and both two-cell examples. Chapter 3 teaches likelihood, score and information before using them; Chapter 4 teaches the physiological pathway and filtering before covariance and MSD tests.

All 23 chapter/section headings were read with their complete sections and sidecar titles. Chapter 3 titles keep the bound as a lower bound, comparisons conditional on fixed quantities, additive errors conditional on assumptions, and the readout limit distinct from abrupt stopping. Chapter 4 titles use points to, challenges, estimates, and can reproduce, matching inferential rather than unique-cause claims. Its measurement-error heading is qualified visibly to positive lags and errors independent of movement and uncorrelated across sampled times; the filtering heading is qualified visibly to stable decaying kernels and nonzero static gain.

Cauchy-Schwarz uses the preceding projected diffusion and tangent normalization. Equality is a proportionality condition at the current state. The exponential rule is visibly sufficient, and the linear counterexample does not alter the inequality. The matrix claim requires invertibility and keeps coupled directions distinct from scalar coordinate checks.

Storage time T and observation time L remain separate. Zero cross covariance follows from local unbiasedness and future-noise independence; translation invariance supplies one readout variance. Independent Gaussian observation and transition noises are visibly identified as an approximation. Naive averaging, backward precision, ideal asymptote, full/partial access and the printed inequality caution remain inside that declared model.

One-neuron-at-a-time recordings are distinguished from simultaneous neuronal covariance. R squared is a fitted linear explanatory fraction; the common fraction uses calibrated unit gain and approximately uncorrelated contributions. The chapter retains the order-1/N private cross term, two-animal/horizontal/350 ms scope and uncertainty limits. Filtered white input and Brownian position are compared under the same one-pole teaching filter before the fuller model. Upstream localization remains separate from proof that integrator neurons are the unique generator.

All nine guide figure and table sidecar entries were read against their source leads and interpretations. Chapter 3 captions separate readout from storage, preserve the positive-rate range and show that a lower bound can fall while actual diffusion stays fixed. Chapter 4 captions separate the physical pathway from analysis, common from predictor noise, positive-lag measurement offsets from zero lag, and independently normalized model shapes from fitted data. No figure or block is inside a fold. This is a content/caption check, not a pixel inspection.

Unchanged full paper calculations and empirical estimates were not rerun. The stage checks the mathematical meaning and conditions of the proposed teaching path and its changes; it does not certify raw-data reproduction or resolve every existing source-paper claim.
